scope: Persisted tenant-owned flow definitions, versions, enablement permissions and intent mappings with database-derived tenant authorization in API and Cloud.

environment.database: Separate disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 databases for API and Cloud on localhost.
environment.fixtures: Synthetic tenant A and B admin accounts, two tenant flow definitions and related configuration only; all UAT-079 rows and users were removed after verification.
environment.restart: Both local services restarted against their same isolated database before readback.
environment.network: Local API/Cloud HTTP and PostgreSQL only; no customer flow or provider endpoint was invoked.

assertions_per_backend: Registration produced ordinary user accounts before isolated database preparation assigned tenant-admin scope for the two synthetic companies.
Each admin created a flow definition while submitting a forged other-company ID; the API persisted the company from the current database actor.
Definition list reads ignored a caller-supplied foreign company filter and returned only the actor's company definitions.
Tenant A updated and archived its definition; a cross-tenant update returned null without authorizing the foreign record.
Admins created draft flow versions with DB-derived creator IDs; a foreign-definition version create returned 400.
Tenant A approved its draft version; editing the approved version returned 400.

Flow enablement permission upsert ignored a forged company ID, persisted under Tenant A, updated enabled=true to false without deleting/replacing the row, and rejected a reference to Tenant B's flow with 400.
Intent-flow mapping upsert ignored a forged company ID, persisted under Tenant A, replaced the prior allowed-flow ID set on update, and rejected Tenant B's flow reference with 400.
After API/Cloud restart, scoped reads returned the archived definition, approved version, disabled-but-retained permission and replacement intent mapping for Tenant A, and excluded Tenant B rows.
Database cleanup removed all UAT-079 accounts, definitions, versions, permissions and mappings; verification found zero named fixture rows.
limitations: This closes the four exercised admin/API matrix rows only; Web, coordinator, superadmin and other-role rows remain open.
No flow was executed against a live call platform, browser integration, CRM or customer endpoint.
